title: Manager's Special: The Best Deal in the Store Has a 4-Hour Window
editorialNotes: Version-stale: this is the pre-Aug-19 7-slide brief; an 8-slide re-brief exists per COVERAGE.md but is not in briefs/.

The $800-1,200/year saving and the 40% markdown are the brief's own estimate with no citation; kept in the headline, never as hero type. The brief visual note (bars $1,560 vs $936 saving $624-800) conflicts with the $800-1,200 claim and is not carried.
Slide 1 line 1 exceeds 8 words per hook line; verbatim from the brief.

thread.endState: 10 PM, full arc, clock slightly enlarged

copy.headline: That yellow sticker doesn't mean the food is bad. It means the store is about to lose money.
copy.body: You're not too late. You're right on time.

copy.headline: "Manager's Special" stickers appear when a product is within 24-48 hours of its sell-by date.
items: The store marks it down to move it before it goes unsellable - not unsafe.
copy.citation: Standard retail markdown practice; USDA food safety guidelines on sell-by dates.

copy.headline: When they appear:
items: Early morning (7-9 AM) when night-crew restocks and dates are checked.
And Sunday evening (5-8 PM) when stores pull product before Monday's delivery.
Hit both windows and you cover the full markdown cycle.

copy.headline: The math: a family buying protein twice weekly, shifting both purchases to Manager's Special windows at a 40% markdown, saves $800-1,200/year on meat alone.
copy.body: No coupons. No apps. Just timing.

copy.headline: How to exploit it:
items: Go to the meat section first, not last.
Stickers are applied in real time - early shoppers get first pick.
Buy what's stickered that fits your week's meals.
Freeze anything you won't use today.

copy.headline: What the store would prefer you not know:
items: The markdown exists to recover partial cost on product the store would otherwise write off at full loss.
If shoppers systemically bought marked-down meat and froze it, the store loses margin per unit.
copy.body: The markdown is the store's Plan B. Make it your Plan A.

copy.headline: The best deal in the grocery store isn't a sale. It's a sticker that appears twice a week at a predictable time.
copy.ctaLine: fond tracks your freezer so you always know what's worth buying when the sticker appears. Link in bio.
